declared_purpose: Provide cultural astrology, divination, relationship, naming, styling and feng-shui readings, with optional profiles, reports and daily notifications (SKILL.md:1-11, 87-119, 176-190). Push and preference learning explicitly require opt-in; local retention and deletion controls are promised (SKILL.md:320-325, 338-377, 411-448). Browser LLM interpretation is an optional disclosure exception. Cron snapshots, outbox files, deletion mechanics and command-output fields are implementation choices.

data_operations.operation: Request inputs according to the selected reading
data_operations.source: User submissions to the host agent
data_operations.data_scope: Question/background; birth date, time, city and sometimes gender; optionally names, both partners' information, naming preferences, body/style descriptions or spatial layout and orientation.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Host-agent conversation; supplying inputs does not itself require profile creation.
data_operations.condition: Depends on the chosen system and requested detail. The routing guide permits lighter readings when information is missing.

data_operations.operation: Accept physical-feature descriptions or optional images
data_operations.source: User-provided palm/face descriptions, photographs, charts or floor plans
data_operations.data_scope: Physical features and potentially identifiable images or home-layout information.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Host-agent conversation. The instructions prohibit automatic profile storage of photographs; host transcript storage is unresolved.
data_operations.condition: Text descriptions are preferred. Photo alternatives require an informed, active request; face-photo intake is restricted to the submitting adult's own image.

data_operations.operation: Calculate readings and infer symbolic personal attributes
data_operations.source: Submitted inputs, derived charts and current or supplied dates
data_operations.data_scope: Charts, compatibility, personality, relationship patterns, financial themes, health/energy themes and life-stage interpretations.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Calculation results return to the invoking caller for interpretation. Standalone output is not evidence of onward disclosure or logging.
data_operations.condition: When the corresponding calculation or interpretation path is selected. Registration separately persists derived analysis.

data_operations.operation: Create and persist a registration profile
data_operations.source: Registration CLI arguments and local calculations
data_operations.data_scope: User ID, name, gender, birth date/time/place, corrected solar date/time/city, derived BaZi and analysis, timestamps, defaults and placeholder family records. Spouse gender is inferred from the registrant's gender.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local data/profiles/<userId>.json; registration also echoes identifying inputs to the caller's stdout.
data_operations.condition: Successful registration requires five positional inputs; omitted birthplace defaults to Shanghai. Push is absent by default; the registration shortcut requires both --push and --i-consent.

data_operations.operation: Read, edit and add profile or family information
data_operations.source: Existing profile JSON and explicitly supplied fields/member details
data_operations.data_scope: Entire profile on reads; arbitrary nested-field updates; family names, relationship, birth details, gender, BaZi and addition dates.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local profile JSON. Mutation confirmations echo supplied values or names to stdout.
data_operations.condition: Profile save/add commands. Paths interpolate userId without a directory-containment check.

data_operations.source: Local profile directory and profile JSON
data_operations.data_scope: Profile IDs, names, birth information, gender, chart information and family details. Defaults mask several fields but retain birth year and gender; the family heading prints the owner's full name.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Invoking caller's stdout/stderr; no packaged onward transmission.
data_operations.condition: show/load/family/list commands. --full exposes additional fields; list enumerates all JSON profiles.

data_operations.operation: Read two profiles for relationship analysis
data_operations.source: Two local profile files, or directly supplied names and BaZi
data_operations.data_scope: Profile mode reads complete records and extracts both names and four pillars; direct-input mode avoids profile reads. OPENCLAW_OWNER_ID may be read as an identity assertion.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process memory and a compatibility report returned through stdout.
data_operations.condition: Two-ID mode accepts --i-am or OPENCLAW_OWNER_ID matching either participant. This is a supplied assertion, not verification of identity or the other participant's consent. Four-input mode uses submitted data.

data_operations.operation: Record interactions, infer topic preferences and clear learning history
data_operations.data_scope: Timestamped topic/context events, up to 500 entries; decayed weights and inferred focusAreas. Topics are restricted, but context is not validated against the four defined categories.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local profile JSON; weights/top results return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Recording requires allowPreferenceLearning === true and an opt-in timestamp. Opt-out clears interactionLog and resets focusAreas; old entries otherwise disappear through count-based rollover.

data_operations.operation: Create notification jobs and retain push settings
data_operations.source: Profile, inferred/default top topics and selected channel/times
data_operations.data_scope: Routing ID/channel/session key, schedules and two prompt snapshots containing name, complete BaZi, day stem and ranked interests; local consent timestamps and cron IDs.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Serialized __OPENCLAW_CRON_ADD__ messages on stdout to OpenClaw; settings in local profile JSON. Runtime storage and downstream model processing are unknown.
data_operations.condition: push-toggle on, including the explicitly consented registration shortcut. These jobs schedule agent prompts calling daily-fortune.js; they do not schedule the standalone daily-push.js path.

data_operations.operation: Instruct scheduled interpretation, delivery and preference recording
data_operations.data_scope: Personalized daily reading and the top topic recorded with morning_push/evening_push context.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: OpenClaw agent/runtime and the configured direct recipient; learning events return to local profiles if learning is enabled.
data_operations.condition: If OpenClaw executes the emitted jobs. Prompts instruct recording after generation, without checking user engagement. Actual execution and delivery are not demonstrated by packaged code.

data_operations.operation: Scan profiles and select standalone push/test targets
data_operations.data_scope: Complete profiles, including family and interaction history, before target filtering. Eligibility checks pushEnabled, an opt-in timestamp and BaZi day/dayStem.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local daily-push.js process memory. --list returns aggregate counts, channel distribution and prior-push counts.
data_operations.condition: Standalone live, dry-run, test and list paths. --test still scans every profile before selecting one user and is forced to dry-run.

data_operations.data_scope: Sanitized user ID, generation timestamp and full reading, including name/gendered salutation, inferred trends and BaZi-derived information. Successful file creation updates lastPushDate.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local data/outbox/<safeId>_<date>.txt, containing JSON; intended for OpenClaw pickup. Directory/file creation requests modes 0700/0600.
data_operations.condition: Live standalone push only. Dry-run/test creates no outbox or profile-date update. A true return establishes file creation, not remote delivery.

data_operations.operation: Persist bounded execution logs and emit diagnostic output
data_operations.data_scope: Run timestamps, statuses and stable eight-hex-character SHA-256 prefixes of user IDs; these are pseudonymous identifiers. Test/loading diagnostics can expose IDs or filenames to the caller.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local data/push-log.json, retaining 100 runs; stdout/stderr diagnostics.
data_operations.condition: Logs are written only in live mode. The live status expression references block-scoped sent outside its block, causing the catch path to record processing_failed after a possible successful outbox write.

data_operations.operation: Disable notifications and delete or retain a profile
data_operations.data_scope: Push consent/settings and the complete profile, including family/history. Default deletion retains the file through renaming; --purge unlinks the active profile.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: __OPENCLAW_CRON_RM__ output to OpenClaw; local profile or .json.deleted-<timestamp> file. The deletion function does not remove outbox or push-log records.
data_operations.condition: Push off updates settings and requests job removal. Profile deletion requires --yes or interactive DELETE confirmation and attempts push disable first. Recovery is described as 30 days, but no expiry enforcement is implemented.

data_operations.operation: Read browser inputs and render local divination
data_operations.source: Question textarea, generated six-line results and runtime API-key/model fields
data_operations.data_scope: Question, hexagram and interpretation in browser memory/DOM. Question text is interpolated into innerHTML. Reset clears casting/output state but retains question and credential inputs.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browser DOM. No localStorage read/write implementation appears in the supplied HTML despite documentation claiming key storage there.
data_operations.condition: After six casts, showResult invokes callLLM automatically. Missing key, cancelled consent, invalid endpoint or request failure selects local fallback.

data_operations.operation: Disclose a browser divination request to the selected LLM provider
data_operations.source: Runtime credential, typed question, derived hexagram and static prompts
data_operations.data_scope: Question, hexagram names/attributes and six yin/yang lines, static instructions, model/settings and LLM API key in the Authorization header. No profile/file/environment data is added by this request constructor.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Selected https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions, https://api.anthropic.com/v1/chat/completions or https://api.deepseek.com/v1/chat/completions. Provider retention is unknown; streamed output returns to the browser.
data_operations.condition: A key is present and the user confirms the per-request dialog. The UI offers three fixed endpoints; executable validation checks HTTPS and known hostnames. Disclosure can occur even if the provider rejects the request.

data_operations.data_scope: Fixed author-local avatar JPEG path, relative maple PNGs and optional font requests; these references do not themselves include profile or question data.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local browser resource loader when opened as a file; hosting origin for root/relative URLs when served over HTTP. Optional font stylesheet recipient is fonts.googleapis.com.
data_operations.condition: Image references are active on page load. Google Fonts links are commented out and require a source edit to activate.

data_operations.operation: Specify optional HTML report generation or saved records
data_operations.data_scope: Chart/question, conclusions, detailed interpretation and suggestions.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Generated report for the caller; exact file destination and retention are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Optional workflow step. No supplied report-writing implementation establishes a specific persistence operation.

potential_excess.data_scope: Every other user's complete profile during a single-user --test invocation.
potential_excess.condition: --test selects its requested user only after loadAllProfiles reads every JSON file.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: A targeted calculation test requires the selected user's data.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Load that profile and perform the forced dry-run calculation.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Replace unrelated profile reads with direct loading of the selected ID. These reads are redundant actions.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep missing-user handling and the prohibition on test delivery/persistence.

potential_excess.data_scope: Family birth details, interaction history and unrelated profile fields during batch eligibility checks and aggregate listing.
potential_excess.condition: Batch/live/dry-run/list paths parse complete profiles before checking a few eligibility fields.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Batch selection needs push consent and minimal chart availability; aggregate listing additionally needs channel/prior-push state.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Select eligible users and calculate their readings.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Maintain minimal selection metadata and load only eligible users' required calculation fields. This narrows data in a necessary selection action.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep consent metadata synchronized and preserve target selection, aggregate counts and personalized output.

potential_excess.data_scope: Name, complete BaZi, day stem and ranked interests duplicated into morning/evening scheduler prompts.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: OpenClaw cron through __OPENCLAW_CRON_ADD__ stdout payloads; runtime persistence is unresolved.
potential_excess.condition: Push enable constructs and emits both personalized prompt snapshots.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Scheduling and routing are required; personalization is required when generating the reading.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Register the two schedules and give the execution component access to necessary personalization data.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Put a profile reference and task type in scheduler metadata; resolve minimal personalization locally at execution time.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: The isolated execution session must retain authorized local-profile access. Preserve schedules, routing and personalized results.

potential_excess.data_scope: Automatically generated morning_push/evening_push events and the interests inferred from them.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: interactionLog and preferences.focusAreas in local profile JSON.
potential_excess.condition: The runtime follows a scheduled prompt and preference learning is enabled; recording follows generation without an engagement signal.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Preference learning is described as learning from user interactions.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Generate and deliver opted-in notifications; learn from actual qualifying interactions.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove generation-only recording, or require an explicit engagement event before recording. The automatic record is a separate, potentially redundant action.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve notification delivery and separately consented learning from user queries or verified engagement.

potential_excess.data_scope: Arbitrary caller-supplied context content beyond the four categorical interaction sources.
potential_excess.condition: An opted-in caller supplies a non-enumerated context; recordInteraction persists it without validation.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The weighting algorithm needs a source category, not unrestricted contextual content.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Record the supported category and apply its multiplier.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Validate context against CONTEXT_MULTIPLIERS and reject or normalize unsupported values before storage.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep all four supported contexts and their existing weighting behavior.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete deleted profiles, including family information and interaction history.
potential_excess.condition: Default confirmed deletion renames the file; no packaged expiry removes it after the advertised recovery period.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain recoverability for that period and support immediate --purge deletion.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Enforce deletion after the recovery period instead of leaving recovery copies without an implemented deadline.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the advertised recovery window, confirmation and immediate purge option.

potential_excess.data_scope: Dated delivery files containing identifiable personalized readings.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local data/outbox/<safeId>_<date>.txt, outside the profile deletion boundary.
potential_excess.condition: Standalone live pushes create files. No packaged acknowledgement cleanup, expiry or profile-deletion cleanup is shown; runtime cleanup remains unknown.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: A local handoff file supports delivery, not necessarily historical retention.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep pending payloads available until delivery and permitted retries finish.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove acknowledged/expired payloads and associated pending files on explicit user deletion; define a bounded retry retention period.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve reliable handoff and retries. Coordinate cleanup with the unresolved OpenClaw pickup protocol.

potential_excess.data_scope: Registration identity/birth inputs, arbitrary updated field values, added family names and the unmasked profile-owner name in family headings.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Invoking caller's stdout. Additional terminal/CI retention exists only if the caller captures it.
potential_excess.condition: Registration and mutation confirmations print raw inputs; family headings print the owner's name even without --full.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Registration/profile management needs confirmation; ordinary masked viewing should honor its masking choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Confirm success and identify the affected operation without repeating sensitive values.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use value-free confirmations and mask the family heading unless --full is selected. These are extra fields in otherwise required responses.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve explicit full inspection and reading reports where personal inputs are part of the requested result.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete BaZi and exact birth date/time in push status output.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Invoking caller's stdout; capture or onward sharing is not established.
potential_excess.condition: push-toggle status always includes these fields without a full-output flag.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Notification status concerns enablement, schedule, route and job IDs.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Return operational push configuration and, if useful, a chart-available indicator.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit birth/chart values from status; leave detailed inspection to profile show --full.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep all information needed to inspect and manage the notification jobs.

potential_excess.data_scope: An assumed spouse gender derived as the opposite of the registrant's gender.
potential_excess.condition: Every registration creates the placeholder, without spouse information being supplied.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Registration and BaZi calculation concern the registrant; family information is optional.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Create the registrant's profile and allow later voluntary family entry.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Leave the spouse record absent or gender blank until supplied; avoid persisting the inferred attribute.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve registration calculations and later optional relationship analysis.

potential_excess.data_scope: User name requested for default life-path numerology.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Host-agent conversation; persistence or external disclosure is not established by the intake table.
potential_excess.condition: The preparation table is followed as mandatory numerology intake, although the specialized framework defaults to Life Path using birth date alone.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Name-based numerology is an optional extension, separate from the default reading.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Collect birth date for Life Path; confirm name spelling only for requested name analysis.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Mark the name optional and conditional on name-based calculations.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep name collection available for explicitly selected name-based numerology.

potential_excess.data_scope: Residential address offered as feng-shui intake.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Host-agent conversation; no address-upload destination is established.
potential_excess.condition: The generic preparation guide's floor-plan/address option is used for basic spatial guidance.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The detailed routing guide requires space type, layout, orientation/openings and improvement goals, without an address.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Obtain sufficient spatial structure and orientation.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Request a de-identified sketch or description and orientation; omit address collection for this supported basic path.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve layout and directional detail needed for the requested reading.

potential_excess.data_scope: Accessible JSON files outside the intended profile directory when userId contains path traversal.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Resolved local filesystem paths and, on viewing paths, the invoking caller.
potential_excess.condition: Several readers/writers interpolate unvalidated userId into path.join. Crafted path components can escape data/profiles; deletion uses the same path construction.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Profile operations need access to the selected user's record within the declared storage directory.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Resolve legitimate user identifiers to contained profile files.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Validate identifiers and enforce resolved-path containment before reads, writes, renames or deletion.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Support legitimate existing identifiers or provide an explicit migration; preserve normal profile operations.

unknowns: OpenClaw implementation is absent: IPC acceptance, cron persistence/removal, model recipients, delivery routing, authentication, outbox pickup/acknowledgement and cleanup cannot be verified. The supplied code establishes handoff requests, not successful delivery or remote deletion.
Host-agent processing and transcript retention are unspecified. Promises that conversation images are discarded at session end cannot establish erasure by the host or its model provider.
LLM-provider retention, training use, onward disclosure, redirects and endpoint compatibility are undocumented. A rejected request can still disclose its submitted payload.
Dependency implementations are not supplied. package-lock.json identifies installation artifacts, but does not establish dependencies' runtime privacy behavior.
Question text reaches innerHTML in the browser. Additional active-content requests depend on supplied markup and browser policy; no fixed additional recipient or payload can be established.

Actual filesystem permissions, backups, terminal capture and external housekeeping are unknown. Source-level unlinking or requested file modes do not establish secure erasure or effective access controls.

Optional HTML-report storage paths and retention are unspecified. The publishing helper and ignore file mentioned in documentation are absent from the inventory, so their behavior or exclusion cannot be verified.
